short: A crucial Russian victory that destroyed a Swedish supply train, crippling Charles XII's invasion of Russia.
full:
Fought on 9 October 1708, the Battle of Lesnaya was a pivotal encounter during the Swedish invasion of Russia. A Russian force led by Peter the Great intercepted a Swedish relief column commanded by General Adam Ludwig Lewenhaupt. The Swedish column was escorting a massive supply train containing crucial ammunition and provisions intended for Charles XII's main army.

After a fierce, day-long struggle in heavy snow, the Swedes were forced to abandon their wagons and retreat. The loss of the supplies severely weakened Charles XII's army just as they faced the brutal winter of 1708–1709, setting the stage for their catastrophic defeat at Poltava the following year.
